questions.q: Why does LWC favor components communicating through events over a child directly calling a method on its parent?
options: Direct coupling makes components fragile -- a change to one component can silently break another; events let the firing component stay independent of who's listening
Direct method calls between components are technically impossible in JavaScript
Events are the only way to pass data of any kind between components
Events execute faster than any direct method call
questions.explain: Firing an event lets a component stay decoupled from whoever is listening, which is what keeps components independently reusable -- direct calls between components create fragile coupling that breaks easily during refactors.

questions.q: Which statement about creating and dispatching a custom event in LWC is correct?
options: Both `CustomEvent` and `dispatchEvent` must be imported from the `lwc` module
`dispatchEvent` must be imported from `lightning/events`
`CustomEvent` is a standard browser global needing no import, and `dispatchEvent` is inherited from `LightningElement`
Custom events can only be created inside a lifecycle hook, never inside a regular method
questions.explain: `CustomEvent` is a native browser API available globally with no import needed, and `dispatchEvent` is inherited from `LightningElement` (ultimately from the native `HTMLElement`), so neither needs an explicit import.

questions.q: Why must custom event names in LWC be lowercase, with no spaces or special characters?
options: Uppercase letters are not technically valid in any JavaScript string
It is purely a style convention Salesforce suggests with no functional consequence
Because HTML attributes and event names are case-insensitive, so an event named with mixed case would be indistinguishable from a differently-cased version to a listener
Lowercase events run faster than mixed-case events
questions.explain: Because HTML is case-insensitive, `recordSelect` and `recordselect` would be indistinguishable to a listener -- which is exactly why the platform convention requires lowercase, single-word event names.

questions.q: What is the `detail` property on a `CustomEvent` used for?
options: Setting the CSS class of the element that dispatched the event
Naming the event itself
Specifying which DOM element the event should bubble up to
Attaching a data payload to the event that a listener can read as `event.detail`
questions.explain: `detail` is the standard, documented place to attach a payload to a CustomEvent -- a listener reads that payload back out through `event.detail`.

questions.q: By default, does a `CustomEvent` dispatched from a component bubble up through the DOM or cross shadow DOM boundaries?
options: Yes to both, by default, with no configuration needed
It bubbles by default but never crosses shadow DOM boundaries, even with composed: true
No to both by default -- `bubbles: true` and `composed: true` must be set explicitly for either behavior
It crosses shadow DOM boundaries by default but never bubbles
questions.explain: By default, a CustomEvent only reaches a listener attached directly to the dispatching element -- it neither bubbles nor crosses shadow DOM boundaries unless `bubbles: true` and `composed: true` are explicitly set.
